questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- the fact that Australia is an english speaking country 
- the courses available at the university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: - I was very happy with my overall experience

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: - the process was quite straightforward, I received all information via E-Mail and the host university provided a lot of information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Every student was assigned to s study coordinator who we could talk to before and after arrival. We had an intro week with a couple of welcome events where we got all information and assisstance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Even tough it was a lot of information and several e-mails to go through, I think the University of Sydney did a good job in providing several resources and assistance during orientation week

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
To find housing in Sydney is pretty tough since it is very expensive and there is not a lot available. It definetely depends on the area you would like to live in but you should calculate with 7500 DKK. I found my first apartment via facebook but the lease was just 8 weeks so I had to look for another apartment after. If you only need a short term lease it is definetely doable and more easy onshore. i used the app
flatmates.com.au
and found a 3 month lease within 2 weeks.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Get the premium version for
flatmates.com.au
and look up facebook etc. I personally prefeered living off campus cause I wanted to live closer to the beach and meet people outside of the uni context. I dont regreat living off campus at all.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Another reason why i chose living off campus was the housing availability for students. The cheapest housing was 350 AUD per week and provided the absolute bar minimum. Everything else was ridicilously expensive (up to 750 AUD per week) and I payed less for a better accomondation off shore. I can see that living on campus provides a community aspect that i didnt have but prices for what you get were not worth it to me.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The initial process (application at the university etc.) was pretty straighforward. The class registration was a bit of a mess but will describe that more below

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After being approved from UCPH I received an "unconditional offer" from Sydney University. To receive my conditional offer I needed to apply again to Sydney University, but the application was fairly easy and not extensive (no new motivation letter etc., just hand in of documents etc.). After receiving my conditional offer, course registration, visa application and things like the student health insurance followed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Study coordinators from Sydney University

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Despite all the help students received, the class registration was quite a mess. I study Global Health and since Sydney University has a global health masters degree I chose the university (the global health classes I found online matched my interests and I was very excited to take them). However, we only got a list with available classes after we went thourgh the entire reigstration process and it turned out that Sydney University has only very limited course availabilites for global health students. I almost dropped my entire exchange cause no classes I wanted to take were available. All exchange students from Sydney University receive a "postgraduate course list" and most of the classes are from degrees like law or engineering etc. I never understood why Sydney University didnt give us a list of available classes BEFORE the registration process so we could have made a decision based on that. It took quite a while but I finally found 4 classes that matched with my study degree and my interests from master degrees like "the sustainability masters degree" or "international relations masters degree". Once I got my classes approved from copenhagen university I thought the process is done but the worst part was yet to happen. In Sydney, you can only see the time of each class AFTER you got approved. So it turned out that 3 of my four classes take place at the same time so all my classes clashed and I couldnt take them. Process began from again and I had to find 3 other classes that took place at a different time. By the time I applied for new classes tho, most of them were already full. With a lot of effort and help of my study coordinator I finally figured out a study plan that fit my interests and worked out with the timeline but it was not what I initially wanted at all. I think as undergad students there is a lot more classes available. I was quite restricted since I also couldnt take any undergrad classes (from copenhagen university side) which made it more complicated.. But i figured it out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask for the postgraduate / undergraduate course list and definetely have a couple of back up courses / a back-up plan in case your classes clash.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: quite satisfied. USYD also has good student wellbeing supports

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: More challenging than some classes I had at copenhagrn university cause the System in Sydney is quite different. Completing 30ects (which is equivalent to 4 classes in Sydney) was definetely a lot of work and my most challenging semester during my masters degree.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Sydney University is more siminlar to the american System than the european. Each course has multiple submissions (each submission counts a specific percentage to the overall grade) so students can expect around 4 submission per class. I had 17 submission in total between August and end of November. Students are more flexible with deciding essay topics and you can get simple extensions (5 days more time) if you have multiple submisison during the week. Overall, students need to reach 50% in order to pass the class so there is less pressure on each exam since multiple count towards the final grade. I liked that the professors gave extensive feedback on each assignment where as at UCPH we only get general feedback / a few comments. There was a rubrik for every assignment with a specific score you could reach so it was very clear to see where your grade was coming from. At UCPH is often seems more random. Therefore, i liked to structured approach at Sydney University and the slightly more interactive teaching style (more disucssions, seminars, tutorial papers etc.)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Food and water security (SUST5002)
- Sustainable Development and population health (SUST5004)
- Globalisation and Governance (GOVT6123)
- Forces of change in international relations (GOVT6137)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I personally liked the globalisation and governance and forces of change course a lot, since it covered topics that I was missing within my masters. The courses were quite political but offered a good perspective about globalisation and its drawbacks / positive aspects and both classes were really interactive and discussion based.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: - not a lot of unexpected costs, a lot of expenses were my personal decision and are very subjective

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
- more expensive: groceries, public transport, gym, travel costs
- less expensive: eating out in restaurants / cafes, there a are ot of things to do for free in Sydney

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: really satisfied. A lot of cool clubs ( i joined the bushwalking club, the photography club and the food lovers club) and sport opportunities!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sydney University had a couple of campus festivals where they introduced clubs students can join, There is a ton of options for everyone and really cool opportunities to get involved. The university also offers a sustainability programm, volunteering opportunities and sport clubs. no complaints here.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked to bushwalking club cause it offers a lot of cheap trips to cool places and is good for socializing. I liked joining yoga classes at the beach to get engaged in Sydney´s morning culture and I also joined a surf camp which was really fun and goof to meet people. There are so many options since Sydney is such a big city where everyone can find something to do.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
- rent a car and go down south to jervis bay / kiama / wollongong 
- go north with the train and visit palm beach and all other northern beaches
- a lot of cool camping opportunities around the east coast and cheap camping stuff to find at k-mart (definetely make your way up to byron bay!)
- I went to tasmania which was amaying and so worth it as well to the ayers rock with a company that organized four days in the outback; doing a padi diving licence at the great barrier reef was my highlight
- however, if the budget is limited there are so  many cool and cheap / free trips from sydney. Public transport is really good and you can just hop in the train and go to the royal nationalpark or all the way up to new castle.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
- pretty easy
- australians are very chatty, friendly and laid-back and the culture is very western / quite americanzed
- a very easy country to adjust to

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: - join clubs, engage in course work / group work

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: - personally, I didnt find cultural differences challenging it was more challenging to actually engage with australians and not only socialize with exchange students. It is very easy to get into this big international bubble and forget socializing with australians but most of them already have their established friend group etc. There are mainly asian students at the campus, so there are not a ton of options to meet a lot of australians at university (at least for the postgraduate courses)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
- very laid back and chilled
- very social and friendly people. I liked that everyone just starts talking to you / australians like to have small talk and I always felt very welcomed

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- be prepared to have quite a lot of university work but also appreciate the campus life and dont get too stressed. The USYD campus is awesome and there are so many ways to engage there as a student and enjoy the cheap coffee all around campus :) 
- Make sure to really enjoy sydney. I know a lot of people who just went from trip to trip and lost track of how beautiful sydney is. It is such an amazing city and definetely worth to spend time there and around it (make sure to visit all the beaches!)
- be prepared to have the financial resources to enjoy it. There are a lot of free things to do but Sydney is very expensive. You are allowed to work as a student so it might be worth it to look into job opportunities. Also be aware that Sydney is really big and you might spend a lot of time in public transport

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: -  I know that undergraduate students had different experiences with that but I found it hard to find "my group of people" in the beginning. Since I attended 4 different courses from 4 different master degrees where everyone already knew each other it was a bit more challenging to socialize. I love that Sydney offers a lot of opportunities to join running clubs / social clubs. I would recommend to participate in those to meet other people as well and have a good time. I also volunteered there (at an asylum seeking center) which was also a really cool experience. Also, make use of the USYD app and get the 25 dollar membership for the semester to make use of free lunch, free coffee etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: - I don´t think there was one single experience that was rewarding. I truly enjoyed studying and having a dails life / routine at a place that always feels like vacation. Sydney definetely opened a new perspecive of how I would like to live in my later life and showed me that a good work / life balance actually does exist. I loved exploring so much and I am still amazed by all the incredible places I saw.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: - getting used to the different university system and the fact that I had constant submissions over a 3 month period

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: - I loved going to Syndey and would absolutely recommend it. It is very hard to get a visa for australia and an exchange is a fairly easy and cool opportunity to explore the country for 6 months. I would have loved to stay longer, Sydney is such a cool place

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
